instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil for the noodles, with 1 tsp of salt in it. Slice a thumb-sized piece of ginger. Separate the white and green parts of the green onions, and chop them. Mince the 2 garlic cloves. Cut the tomatoes into 1-inch pieces, and cut the carrot into thin half-moons.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the ginger and the white parts of the green onions and cook for 30 seconds, until fragrant. Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes and carrot with a pinch of salt. Cover and cook for 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until the tomatoes have broken down. Stir in the 1 tbsp tomato paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add the 6 cups chicken stock, the 2 tbsp soy sauce and the 1 tsp sugar. Bring to a boil, then turn the heat down and simmer, partly covered, for 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, cook the noodles in the boiling water for the time on the package. Drain, rinse under cold water and drain again. Divide them between 4 bowls.
Beat the 4 eggs in a small bowl. Turn the soup up to a rolling boil. Pour the eggs in slowly in a thin stream, stirring gently, then take the pot off the heat right away.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Ladle the soup over the noodles. Top with the green parts of the green onions and a few drops of sesame oil. Serve hot.

For lunches, keep the soup and noodles in separate containers. The soup keeps in the fridge for 3 days and the noodles for 2. Bring the soup to a boil on the stove or reheat it in the microwave until steaming, then pour it over the noodles.
method_notes: None of the versions read shows a rating (Omnivore's Cookbook shows 5 from 8 votes, too few to lead), so the lead is a best-read real version, Foodiebaker. Red House Spice was blocked (403) and was not read. The versions agree on cooking tomatoes down with ginger and green onion, adding stock and soy, and pouring beaten egg into the boiling soup, with noodles cooked separately. They differ on the egg (stirred in strands, fried first, or poached) and on extras like tomato paste, bok choy and oyster sauce. This follows Foodiebaker doubled for 4, adds the tomato paste from Omnivore's Cookbook for depth and leaves out the lettuce.
